Arabinoxylans are the predominant hemicellulose polysaccharide in cereals. Glucose is a minor constituent because the pentoses

Digestion of glucose and its polymers
Digestion of sugars
Most carbohydrates must be broken down to monosaccharides during digestion, but monosaccharides are ready for absorption
upon ingestion. All sugars are digested quickly as they travel to the stomach where they mix with gastric acid and stomach contents.
They become part of chyme, which leaves the stomach through the pylorus into the duodenum. There, monosaccharides can be
absorbed quickly, especially if in liquid or little fat or protein is present.
